diagnosis.root_cause: Infrastructure upgrade caused ingress-controller to ignore legacy annotation 'route.class' in version 4.x, rendering 42 route rules inactive and causing 40% of services to return 503 errors.
evidence: edge-ingress / http_5xx_rate metric spiked at 16:03 UTC from 0.004 to over 0.40
ingress-controller / active_route_rules dropped from ~105 to ~62 at 16:03 UTC
ingress-controller log at 16:02 UTC: 42 route rules did not match any backend after upgrade (legacy annotation 'route.class' ignored in 4.x)
ingress-controller log at 16:05 UTC: 40% of configured routes inactive; affected services returning 503
diagnosis.recommended_fix: Update the ingress route configurations to remove or replace the legacy annotation 'route.class' with the current 4.x standard to restore the inactive route rules.

evidence.plan_reasoning: Since ~40% of services are returning 503 errors and edge-ingress has an http_5xx_rate metric, checking that metric will help us understand the timing and scale of the ingress failures.
We confirmed that edge-ingress http_5xx_rate spikes starting around 16:03 UTC. We should search the logs of edge-ingress to see the specific error messages and understand why requests are failing.
Since edge-ingress has no logs matching '503', we should check the ingress-controller's active_route_rules metric to see if routing configuration or rules changed around 16:03 UTC.

We see active_route_rules drop abruptly around 16:03 UTC, coinciding with the 5xx spike on edge-ingress. We should search the logs of ingress-controller to understand why route rules were dropped or if config-cache failed.
